To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maltose transport protein MalE does not modulate maltoporin as general outer membrane porins.

the malE gene is not essential for the function of maltoporin in maltodextrin transport and that the malE allele has no effect on the activity of maltose-binding protein as an outer membrane porin for the facilitated diffusion and uptake of lactose.
the maltose binding protein does not modify the activity of the maltoporin in Eschericia coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of maltose transport in Escherichiocoli.
the interaction of the outer membrane protein, maltoporin, with the periplasmic protein, maltose-binding protein (MBP).
the interaction between maltoporin and the maltose-binding proteins in Escherichria coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of the maltose-binding proteins with maltoporin is not a general gating mechanism which modulates the diffusion of nonsubstrates of the maltose system.

the maltose transport pathway is a highly specific and efficient mechanism for maltodextrin transport, whereas maltoporin is a general porin which allows the diffusion of a broad variety of solutes, including nonmaltodextrans.
the maltose binding protein does not affect the permeability of maltoporin, at least not in the presence of maltodextrins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of maltose-binding protein with maltoporin is not necessary for the function of the maltose system.
maltoporin is an efficient general outer membrane porine which, in the presence of the maltose-binding proteins, is able to discriminate between substrates.
maltoporin has a high affinity for maltodextrin and a low but significant affinity for other sugars, including lactose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maltose system is not as complex as previously thought and that it can be used as a model system to investigate the molecular mechanism of transport through porins.
